findings.title: Stale denial cache can keep newly granted access denied until TTL
findings.body: The denial cache entry is consulted before any permission evaluation (lines 116-121), but it is only written when a DB-backed check returns false (lines 153-155). When a later DB check would return true, no code deletes the existing denial entry. Thus a user/resource that was denied once (e.g., before permission propagation completed) will continue to receive Allowed: false for shortCacheTTL (30s), even though fresh permissions now allow access. This undermines the PR's goal of letting creators see newly created resources and can cause support issues. Consider deleting the denial key when a fresh check yields allowed, or not caching denials for resources that may be newly created.

findings.title: Denial cache key is ambiguous and omits identity type
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates namespace, userUID, action, name, and parent with '_'. Fields are not escaped and the identity type is not included. Different tuples can collide (e.g., action "a_b", name "c" vs action "a", name "b_c"), and anonymous:0 can collide with user:0. Because this key is checked before permission evaluation in Check, a collision can make a legitimate request return Allowed: false. Use a length-prefixed/JSON-encoded key or include identity type and unambiguous delimiters.

findings.title: Real errors from cached permission lookup are ignored and DB is queried twice
findings.body: In Check, getCachedIdentityPermissions returns cache.ErrNotFound on a cache miss, but it can also return real errors (e.g., GetUserIdentifiers DB failure or unsupported identity type). The code treats any non-nil error as a cache miss and proceeds to getIdentityPermissions, which will perform the same DB/identity lookup again. On transient DB errors this doubles load and can hide the underlying failure from logs. Distinguish errors.Is(err, cache.ErrNotFound) from other errors and return immediately for real errors.
